research_goal: Decide how to implement a product split that turns the desktop app into a Git workspace tracker while moving agent/tool/runtime platform capabilities to agent-platform.
coding_context: Existing Tauri/Next.js workspace monitor with TypeScript snapshot collector, React UI, product/view registries, and Node-based readiness tests.
source_value_provenance: Git official docs establish repository/worktree/submodule boundaries.
Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Antigravity official docs establish that AI coding tools can attach through CLI, IDE, or agent-manager surfaces.
AWS AgentCore official docs establish that runtime, gateway, identity, and tool management are a separate agent platform capability.
Local registries and tests establish how the current desktop app exposes product features and view modes.
plan_evidence: The product split registry maps primary desktop responsibilities to Git workspace import/open/clone/create and current work reports.
The view mode registry hides agent/tool/runtime management from the default user mode.
Workspace monitor tests assert the new navigation, command recommendations, snapshot fields, and separated advanced sections.
stack_version_constraints: Use existing package-lock/pnpm workspace versions in platform-desktop-app.
Do not add new dependencies in this slice.
Keep Tauri v2/Rust desktop shell unchanged.
issue_discussion_notes: Community posts were treated as weak usability/risk signals only: users can be confused when IDE, agent manager, and terminal surfaces are split or malfunctioning.
No product decision relies on Reddit as factual proof; official docs and local tests drive the implemented boundary.
community_signal_notes: Comments and activity indicate discovery of terminal and split-surface confusion, but they are not proof of product behavior.
The practical mitigation is to make separated surfaces explicit in UI labels and registries.
language_options: TypeScript/React renderer and Node collector changes
selected_language: TypeScript/React renderer and Node collector changes
language_decision_notes: The change is primarily product classification, snapshot shaping, and renderer navigation, all already owned by TypeScript/React and Node collector code.
Rust/Tauri changes would add runtime risk without solving the product boundary problem in this slice.
Keeping existing languages avoids new dependencies and keeps tests close to existing workspace monitor coverage.
code_reference_notes: Existing feature panels use compact typed props and data attributes that tests can assert.
Collector already reads JSON registries and sanitizes customer snapshot data, so product split data belongs there.
Readiness tests protect product copy and registry roles, so they should be updated with the boundary change.
architecture_practitioner_sources: Cursor shell command and CLI docs as practical adapter examples
Claude Code CLI docs as terminal-first practical adapter example
Antigravity docs and community split-surface discussions as practical UX risk signals
architecture_options: All-in-one desktop app owns workspaces, agents, tools, model runtime, and provider execution.
Split architecture: desktop app owns Git workspace tracking and guest AI tool launch; agent-platform owns agent/tool/model/runtime capabilities.
Hard fork a full IDE/workbench and make it the main host.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected the split architecture because the user's stated goal is easy use of many AI coding tools over Git workspaces, not a single all-in-one agent runtime console.
Rejected all-in-one because it keeps first-run UI complex and mixes user task tracking with platform/tool construction.
Rejected hard-fork IDE work for this slice because it is a separate project boundary and does not immediately fix the current desktop app's product confusion.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Theory and official docs support modular boundaries: Git repositories are durable work units, while AgentCore-like services are runtime/tool/identity infrastructure.
Practitioner signals show that split surfaces can confuse users unless labels and default navigation make the split explicit.
The selected design keeps advanced capability links visible but removes them from the default user path.
folder_structure_options: Keep all new split contracts inside platform-desktop-app only.
Put desktop tracker contracts in platform-desktop-app and separated agent/tool platform contracts in agent-platform and project registry.
Create a brand-new root project immediately for every separated capability.
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected a two-project boundary using existing root projects: platform-desktop-app for workspace tracker, agent-platform for reusable agent/tool/runtime platform.
A new root repository per user workspace is a product behavior to model and import, not a source folder to add to this monorepo in this slice.
The split registry lives under platform-desktop-app/configs because it drives desktop UI and snapshot output.
folder_semantics_notes: platform-desktop-app/renderer/workspace-monitor contains the user-facing tracker UI and collector.
agent-platform/configs owns reusable platform, view, workflow, agent, tool, and runtime governance.
_history and _requirements retain cross-project evidence and close-out records.
maintainability_notes: A self-documenting registry makes the split inspectable without reading React code.
Snapshot-level split data prevents duplicated product-boundary logic across UI components.
Tests assert labels, navigation, and snapshot fields so future agent/tool features cannot silently return to the default user surface.
findings: Users need Git workspace visibility and report/evidence ordering more than a first-run agent factory.
AI coding tools should attach as optional adapters because Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Antigravity expose different local surfaces.
AgentCore-style functionality is infrastructure/platform work and belongs outside the default desktop tracker path.
options: Keep current agent capability platform direction.
Switch desktop app to workspace tracker and separate agent/tool runtime features.
Create a new desktop app from scratch.
recommendation: Switch desktop app to workspace_tracker now, keep agent/tool/model/runtime functions in agent-platform, and encode the split in registries, snapshot data, UI, and tests.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Official docs and local source confirmed that Git workspaces and AI coding tools can be represented as separate import/guest adapter boundaries, while AgentCore-like capabilities are runtime/tool infrastructure.
post_research_answers.best_option: Split desktop tracker and agent/tool runtime platform.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It reduces first-run complexity and matches the user's core workflow: choose a Git repo, run a tool, and inspect current work outputs.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: All-in-one keeps the confusion; a new app from scratch delays visible repair; a hard-fork IDE is a separate project with larger risk.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Update product/view registries, collector snapshot schema, home/navigation/task-intent UI, feature panels, tests, README, requirements, and specs.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: Physical remote repository creation/import flows and per-tool installation automation remain deeper runtime work.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Run config contract checks, workspace monitor check/test/build, platform desktop test/check, collector, omission/resource/evaluator, and diff checks.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: Product split registry and coding research record document the boundary for future slices.
post_research_answers.next_action: Implement registry, snapshot, UI, tests, and close-out records.

risks_or_unknowns: MonitorShell remains large and should continue to be componentized in follow-up slices.
Actual clone/create remote repository UX is not fully implemented in this slice.
Guest AI tool adapters still depend on each tool's local installation and account state.
